sanskrit: adharmaṃ dharmam ity āhur ye ca mohavaśaṃ gatāḥ avratā naṣṭamaryādās te proktā brahmarākṣasāḥ
english: Those who, fallen under the sway of delusion, call unrighteousness righteousness — men devoid of vows, who have cast off all bounds of conduct — they are declared to be brahma-rākṣasas.

sanskrit: te cet kālakṛtodyogāt saṃbhavantīha mānuṣāḥ nirhomā nirvaṣaṭkārās te bhavanti narādhamāḥ
english: And if, through the working of time, such ones are born here as human beings, they become the lowest of men, performing no oblations and uttering no sacred vaṣaṭ-calls.

sanskrit: eṣa devi mayā sarvaḥ saṃśayacchedanāya te kuśalākuśalo nṝṇāṃ vyākhyāto dharmasāgaraḥ
english: Thus, O goddess, to resolve your doubt I have expounded to you in full this ocean of dharma — the good and the evil deeds of men.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca parāvarajñe dharmajñe tapovananivāsini sādhvi subhru sukeśānte himavatparvatātmaje
english: Maheśvara said: O knower of high and low, O knower of dharma, O dweller in the penance-grove, O virtuous one of lovely brows and beautiful tresses, O daughter of the Himavat mountain —

sanskrit: dakṣe śamadamopete nirmame dharmacāriṇi pṛcchāmi tvāṃ varārohe pṛṣṭā vada mamepsitam
english: O skillful one, endowed with calm and self-restraint, free of selfishness, walker in the path of dharma — I ask you, O fair-hipped one; being asked, tell me what I desire to know.

sanskrit: sāvitrī brahmaṇaḥ sādhvī kauśikasya śacī satī mārtaṇḍajasya dhūmorṇā ṛddhir vaiśravaṇasya ca
english: Sāvitrī is the chaste wife of Brahmā, Śacī the faithful wife of Kauśika (Indra), Dhūmorṇā of Yama the son of Mārtaṇḍa, and Ṛddhi of Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera);

sanskrit: varuṇasya tato gaurī sūryasya ca suvarcalā rohiṇī śaśinaḥ sādhvī svāhā caiva vibhāvasoḥ
english: Gaurī is the wife of Varuṇa, Suvarcalā of Sūrya, the faithful Rohiṇī of the Moon, and Svāhā of Agni the radiant;

sanskrit: aditiḥ kaśyapasyātha sarvās tāḥ patidevatāḥ pṛṣṭāś copāsitāś caiva tās tvayā devi nityaśaḥ
english: and Aditi of Kaśyapa — all of these revere their husbands as gods, and all of them, O goddess, you have ever questioned and waited upon.

sanskrit: tena tvāṃ paripṛcchāmi dharmajñe dharmavādini strīdharmaṃ śrotum icchāmi tvayodāhṛtam āditaḥ
english: Therefore I question you, O knower of dharma, O speaker of dharma: I wish to hear the duty of women, expounded by you from the beginning.

sanskrit: sahadharmacarī me tvaṃ samaśīlā samavratā samānasāravīryā ca tapas tīvraṃ kṛtaṃ ca te tvayā hy ukto viśeṣeṇa pramāṇatvam upaiṣyati
english: You are my partner in dharma, equal to me in conduct, equal in vows, equal in essence and might, and fierce penance has been performed by you; therefore what is spoken by you in particular will attain the standing of authority.

sanskrit: striyaś caiva viśeṣeṇa strījanasya gatiḥ sadā gaur gāṃ gacchati suśroṇi lokeṣv eṣā sthitiḥ sadā
english: And women in particular are ever the refuge of womankind: as a cow goes after a cow, O fair-hipped one, such is forever the way of things in the worlds.

sanskrit: mama cārdhaṃ śarīrasya mama cārdhād viniḥsṛtā surakāryakarī ca tvaṃ lokasaṃtānakāriṇī
english: You are half of my body, and from my half you came forth; you are the doer of the gods' work and the continuer of the world's lineage.

sanskrit: tava sarvaḥ suviditaḥ strīdharmaḥ śāśvataḥ śubhe tasmād aśeṣato brūhi strīdharmaṃ vistareṇa me
english: The whole of the eternal duty of women is well known to you, O auspicious one; therefore declare to me the duty of women fully and in detail.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan sarvabhūteśa bhūtabhavyabhavodbhava tvatprabhāvād iyaṃ deva vāk caiva pratibhāti me
english: Umā said: O Lord, O sovereign of all beings, O source of what has been, what shall be, and what is — by your power alone, O god, does this speech rise up within me.

sanskrit: imās tu nadyo deveśa sarvatīrthodakair yutāḥ upasparśanahetos tvā samīpasthā upāsate
english: But these rivers, O lord of gods, charged with the waters of all sacred fords, stand near and wait upon you for the sake of their cleansing touch.

sanskrit: etābhiḥ saha saṃmantrya pravakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ prabhavan yo 'nahaṃvādī sa vai puruṣa ucyate
english: Having taken counsel together with these, I shall declare it in due order; for he who, though powerful, speaks without egotism — he indeed is called a true man.

sanskrit: strī ca bhūteśa satataṃ striyam evānudhāvati mayā saṃmānitāś caiva bhaviṣyanti saridvarāḥ
english: And a woman, O lord of beings, ever follows after a woman; moreover these foremost rivers will be honored by my doing so.

sanskrit: eṣā sarasvatī puṇyā nadīnām uttamā nadī prathamā sarvasaritāṃ nadī sāgaragāminī
english: This holy Sarasvatī is the highest of rivers, first among all streams, a river that flows to the sea;

sanskrit: vipāśā ca vitastā ca candrabhāgā irāvatī śatadrur devikā sindhuḥ kauśikī gomatī tathā
english: and the Vipāśā, the Vitastā, the Candrabhāgā, the Irāvatī, the Śatadru, the Devikā, the Sindhu, the Kauśikī, and the Gomatī as well;

sanskrit: tathā devanadī ceyaṃ sarvatīrthābhisaṃvṛtā gaganād gāṃ gatā devī gaṅgā sarvasaridvarā
english: and this divine river too, encompassed by all sacred fords, the goddess Gaṅgā who descended from heaven to earth, the foremost of all streams.

sanskrit: ity uktvā devadevasya patnī dharmabhṛtāṃ varā smitapūrvam ivābhāṣya sarvās tāḥ saritas tadā
english: Having spoken thus, the consort of the God of gods, foremost of the upholders of dharma, then addressed all those rivers as if with a smile,

sanskrit: apṛcchad devamahiṣī strīdharmaṃ dharmavatsalā strīdharmakuśalās tā vai gaṅgādyāḥ saritāṃ varāḥ
english: and the queen of the god, devoted to dharma, asked them of the duty of women — those foremost streams, Gaṅgā and the rest, who were skilled in the duty of women.

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhagavatā dattaḥ praśnaḥ strīdharmasaṃśritaḥ taṃ tu saṃmantrya yuṣmābhir vaktum icchāmi śaṃkare
english: "This question concerning the duty of women has been put by the Lord; having taken counsel with you, I wish to answer it to Śaṃkara."

sanskrit: na caikasādhyaṃ paśyāmi vijñānaṃ bhuvi kasya cit divi vā sāgaragamās tena vo mānayāmy aham
english: "For I see that perfect knowledge is to be attained by no single being's effort alone, on earth or in heaven, O ocean-going ones; therefore do I honor you."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ sarvāḥ saricchreṣṭhāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ puṇyatamāḥ śivāḥ tato devanadī gaṅgā niyuktā pratipūjya tām
english: Bhīṣma said: When all those most holy and auspicious rivers, foremost of streams, had thus been questioned, the divine river Gaṅgā, being charged with the answer, after honoring the goddess,

sanskrit: bahvībhir buddhibhiḥ sphītā strīdharmajñā śucismitā śailarājasutāṃ devīṃ puṇyā pāpāpahāṃ śivām
english: abounding in many insights, knowing the duty of women, of pure smile — that holy one, remover of sin, auspicious — addressed the goddess, daughter of the king of mountains;

sanskrit: buddhyā vinayasaṃpannā sarvajñānaviśāradā sasmitaṃ bahubuddhyāḍhyā gaṅgā vacanam abravīt
english: endowed with intellect and modesty, accomplished in all branches of knowledge, rich in much wisdom, Gaṅgā spoke these words with a smile.

sanskrit: dhanyāḥ smo 'nugṛhītāḥ smo devi dharmaparāyaṇā yā tvaṃ sarvajaganmānyā nadīr mānayase 'naghe
english: "Blessed are we, favored are we, O goddess devoted to dharma, that you, honored by the whole world, should honor mere rivers, O sinless one."

sanskrit: prabhavan pṛcchate yo hi saṃmānayati vā punaḥ nūnaṃ janam aduṣṭātmā paṇḍitākhyāṃ sa gacchati
english: "He who, though powerful, questions others or shows them honor — such a one, surely of untainted heart, attains the name of a wise man."

sanskrit: jñānavijñānasaṃpannān ūhāpohaviśāradān pravaktṝn pṛcchate yo 'nyān sa vai nā padam arcchati
english: "He who questions others — men endowed with knowledge and discernment, skilled in reasoning and refutation, fit to expound — he indeed attains the highest station."

sanskrit: anyathā bahubuddhyāḍhyo vākyaṃ vadati saṃsadi anyathaiva hy ahaṃmānī durbalaṃ vadate vacaḥ
english: "In one way the man rich in much wisdom speaks his word in the assembly; in quite another the egotist utters feeble speech."

sanskrit: divyajñāne divi śreṣṭhe divyapuṇye sadotthite tvam evārhasi no devi strīdharmam anuśāsitum
english: "O you of divine knowledge, supreme in heaven, of divine merit, ever exalted — you alone, O goddess, are fit to instruct us in the duty of women."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sārādhitā devī gaṅgayā bahubhir guṇaiḥ prāha sarvam aśeṣeṇa strīdharmaṃ surasundarī
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the goddess, propitiated by Gaṅgā with her many virtues — that fairest of the celestials — declared in full and without omission the whole duty of women.

sanskrit: strīdharmo māṃ prati yathā pratibhāti yathāvidhi tam ahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi tathaiva prathito bhavet
english: "As the duty of women appears to me according to the ordinance, that I shall proclaim, that it may be made widely known just so."

sanskrit: strīdharmaḥ pūrva evāyaṃ vivāhe bandhubhiḥ kṛtaḥ sahadharmacarī bhartur bhavaty agnisamīpataḥ
english: "This duty of a woman is first laid upon her by her kinsmen at the wedding: in the presence of the sacred fire she becomes her husband's partner in dharma."

sanskrit: susvabhāvā suvacanā suvṛttā sukhadarśanā ananyacittā sumukhī bhartuḥ sā dharmacāriṇī
english: "Of good nature, gentle of speech, of good conduct, pleasant to behold, with mind fixed on none but her husband, fair of face — such a one is a woman walking in dharma."

sanskrit: sā bhaved dharmaparamā sā bhaved dharmabhāginī devavat satataṃ sādhvī yā bhartāraṃ prapaśyati
english: "She becomes supreme in dharma, she becomes a partaker of dharma — that virtuous one who ever looks upon her husband as upon a god."

sanskrit: śuśrūṣāṃ paricāraṃ ca devavad yā karoti ca nānyabhāvā hy avimanāḥ suvratā sukhadarśanā
english: "She who renders service and attendance to him as to a god, with no other feeling, untroubled in mind, steadfast in her vows, pleasant to behold —"

sanskrit: putravaktram ivābhīkṣṇaṃ bhartur vadanam īkṣate yā sādhvī niyatācārā sā bhaved dharmacāriṇī
english: "she who gazes upon her husband's face again and again as upon the face of her son, virtuous and disciplined in conduct — she is a woman walking in dharma."

sanskrit: śrutvā daṃpatidharmaṃ vai sahadharmakṛtaṃ śubham ananyacittā sumukhī bhartuḥ sā dharmacāriṇī
english: "Having heard the auspicious duty of husband and wife, ordained as their shared dharma, she who is single-minded and fair of face toward her husband is a woman walking in dharma."

sanskrit: paruṣāṇy api coktā yā dṛṣṭā vā krūracakṣuṣā suprasannamukhī bhartur yā nārī sā pativratā
english: "The woman who, even when addressed with harsh words or looked upon with a cruel eye, keeps a serene face toward her husband — she is devoted to her lord."

sanskrit: na candrasūryau na taruṃ puṃnāmno yā nirīkṣate bhartṛvarjaṃ varārohā sā bhaved dharmacāriṇī
english: "She who, save her husband, gazes not upon the moon, the sun, or a tree bearing a masculine name — that fair-hipped one is a woman walking in dharma."

sanskrit: daridraṃ vyādhitaṃ dīnam adhvanā parikarśitam patiṃ putram ivopāste sā nārī dharmabhāginī
english: "The woman who tends a husband poor, sick, wretched, or worn out by the road, as though he were her son — she is a partaker of dharma."

sanskrit: yā nārī prayatā dakṣā yā nārī putriṇī bhavet patipriyā patiprāṇā sā nārī dharmabhāginī
english: "The woman who is pure and capable, the woman who bears sons, who holds her husband dear and makes him her very life — she is a partaker of dharma."

sanskrit: śuśrūṣāṃ paricaryāṃ ca karoty avimanāḥ sadā supratītā vinītā ca sā nārī dharmabhāginī
english: "She who renders service and attendance ever with untroubled mind, of good cheer and modest bearing — she is a partaker of dharma."

sanskrit: na kāmeṣu na bhogeṣu naiśvarye na sukhe tathā spṛhā yasyā yathā patyau sā nārī dharmabhāginī
english: "She whose longing is set not on pleasures, nor on enjoyments, nor on lordship, nor on comfort, but upon her husband alone — she is a partaker of dharma."

sanskrit: kalyotthānaratā nityaṃ guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratā susaṃmṛṣṭakṣayā caiva gośakṛtkṛtalepanā
english: "Devoted ever to rising at dawn, intent upon the service of her elders, keeping her dwelling well swept and plastered with cow-dung,"

sanskrit: agnikāryaparā nityaṃ sadā puṣpabalipradā devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ nirupya patinā saha
english: "ever intent upon the fire-rite, always offering flowers and oblations, and having set apart, together with her husband, food for the gods, guests, and dependents,"

sanskrit: śeṣānnam upabhuñjānā yathānyāyaṃ yathāvidhi tuṣṭapuṣṭajanā nityaṃ nārī dharmeṇa yujyate
english: "the woman who eats what remains, as is right and ordained, keeping her household ever content and well-nourished — she is joined with dharma."

sanskrit: śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ pādau toṣayantī guṇānvitā mātāpitṛparā nityaṃ yā nārī sā tapodhanā
english: "The woman endowed with virtue who gladdens the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law, and is ever devoted to mother and father — she is rich in penance."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān durbalānāthān dīnāndhakṛpaṇāṃs tathā bibharty annena yā nārī sā pativratabhāginī
english: "The woman who nourishes with food the brāhmaṇas, the weak and helpless, the wretched, the blind and the destitute — she partakes of the merit of a faithful wife."

sanskrit: vrataṃ carati yā nityaṃ duścaraṃ laghusattvayā paticittā patihitā sā pativratabhāginī
english: "She who ever keeps a vow hard for the frail of nature to perform, her thoughts upon her husband and devoted to his welfare — she partakes of the merit of a faithful wife."

sanskrit: puṇyam etat tapaś caiva svargaś caiṣa sanātanaḥ yā nārī bhartṛparamā bhaved bhartṛvratā śivā
english: "This is merit, this is penance, and this is the eternal heaven — for the woman who holds her husband supreme, vowed to her husband, and auspicious."

sanskrit: patir hi devo nārīṇāṃ patir bandhuḥ patir gatiḥ patyā samā gatir nāsti daivataṃ vā yathā patiḥ
english: "For the husband is the god of women, the husband their kinsman, the husband their refuge; there is no refuge equal to the husband, nor any deity like unto him."

sanskrit: patiprasādaḥ svargo vā tulyo nāryā na vā bhavet ahaṃ svargaṃ na hīccheyaṃ tvayy aprīte maheśvara
english: "For a woman the favor of her husband and heaven itself may be of equal worth — or rather, I would not even desire heaven if you were displeased, O Maheśvara."

sanskrit: yady akāryam adharmaṃ vā yadi vā prāṇanāśanam patir brūyād daridro vā vyādhito vā kathaṃ cana
english: "Should a husband, whether poor or sick, ever in any wise command what ought not be done, or what is contrary to dharma, or even what would destroy life —"

sanskrit: āpanno ripusaṃstho vā brahmaśāpārdito 'pi vā āpaddharmān anuprekṣya tat kāryam aviśaṅkayā
english: "or if he be in distress, fallen into enemy hands, or even afflicted by a brāhmaṇa's curse — then, regarding the duties proper to times of calamity, that is to be done without hesitation."

sanskrit: eṣa deva mayā proktaḥ strīdharmo vacanāt tava yā tv evaṃbhāvinī nārī sā bhaved dharmabhāginī
english: "Thus, O god, at your bidding I have declared the duty of women; and the woman who is of such a disposition becomes a partaker of dharma."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tu deveśaḥ pratipūjya gireḥ sutām lokān visarjayām āsa sarvair anucaraiḥ saha
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the lord of gods, having honored the daughter of the mountain, dismissed the worlds together with all their attendants.

sanskrit: tato yayur bhūtagaṇāḥ saritaś ca yathāgatam gandharvāpsarasaś caiva praṇamya śirasā bhavam
english: Then the hosts of beings and the rivers departed as they had come, and the gandharvas and apsarases too, bowing their heads to Bhava (Śiva).

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā dharmān aśeṣeṇa pāvanāni ca sarvaśaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śāṃtanavaṃ punar evābhyabhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the duties in full and all the means of purification, Yudhiṣṭhira spoke once again to the son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: kim ekaṃ daivataṃ loke kiṃ vāpy ekaṃ parāyaṇam stuvantaḥ kaṃ kam arcantaḥ prāpnuyur mānavāḥ śubham
english: "What is the one deity in the world? What too is the one supreme refuge? By praising whom, by worshipping whom, may men attain blessedness?"

sanskrit: ko dharmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ bhavataḥ paramo mataḥ kiṃ japan mucyate jantur janmasaṃsārabandhanāt
english: "What dharma, of all dharmas, do you hold to be the highest? By murmuring what may a creature be freed from the bondage of birth and the round of existence?"

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca jagatprabhuṃ devadevam anantaṃ puruṣottamam stuvan nāmasahasreṇa puruṣaḥ satatotthitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: The Lord of the universe, the God of gods, the infinite, the Supreme Person — praising him with his thousand names, a man ever vigilant,

sanskrit: tam eva cārcayan nityaṃ bhaktyā puruṣam avyayam dhyāyan stuvan namasyaṃś ca yajamānas tam eva ca
english: and worshipping that same imperishable Person constantly with devotion, meditating, praising, bowing down, and offering sacrifice to him alone —

sanskrit: anādinidhanaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram lokādhyakṣaṃ stuvan nityaṃ sarvaduḥkhātigo bhavet
english: praising forever Viṣṇu, without beginning or end, the great Lord of all worlds, the overseer of the worlds — he passes beyond all sorrow.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaṃ sarvadharmajñaṃ lokānāṃ kīrtivardhanam lokanāthaṃ mahad bhūtaṃ sarvabhūtabhavodbhavam
english: He who is devoted to the brahman, who knows all dharmas, the increaser of the renown of the worlds, the Lord of the worlds, the Great Being, the origin of the becoming of all beings —

sanskrit: eṣa me sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmo 'dhikatamo mataḥ yad bhaktyā puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ stavair arcen naraḥ sadā
english: this I hold to be the highest of all dharmas — that a man should ever worship with hymns, in devotion, the lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: paramaṃ yo mahat tejaḥ paramaṃ yo mahat tapaḥ paramaṃ yo mahad brahma paramaṃ yaḥ parāyaṇam
english: He who is the supreme great splendor, who is the supreme great penance, who is the supreme great brahman, who is the supreme refuge;

sanskrit: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ yo maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam daivataṃ devatānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ yo 'vyayaḥ pitā
english: who is the purifier of things pure and the auspiciousness of things auspicious, the deity of deities, and the imperishable father of all beings;

sanskrit: yataḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhavanty ādiyugāgame yasmiṃś ca pralayaṃ yānti punar eva yugakṣaye
english: from whom all beings come into being at the dawn of the first age, and into whom they pass to their dissolution again at the ending of the age —

sanskrit: tasya lokapradhānasya jagannāthasya bhūpate viṣṇor nāmasahasraṃ me śṛṇu pāpabhayāpaham
english: hear from me, O lord of the earth, the thousand names of that Viṣṇu, the foremost of the worlds, the Lord of the universe — names that drive away sin and fear.

sanskrit: yāni nāmāni gauṇāni vikhyātāni mahātmanaḥ ṛṣibhiḥ parigītāni tāni vakṣyāmi bhūtaye
english: Those descriptive names of the great-souled one that are renowned and have been sung by the seers — those I shall declare for your welfare.

sanskrit: viśvaṃ viṣṇur vaṣaṭkāro bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ bhūtakṛd bhūtabhṛd bhāvo bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ
english: The Universe; Viṣṇu; the Vaṣaṭ-utterance; Lord of what has been, shall be, and now is; Maker of beings; Sustainer of beings; pure Being; the Self of beings; the Nurturer of beings;

sanskrit: pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño 'kṣara eva ca
english: the Purified Self, and the Supreme Self; the highest goal of the liberated; the Imperishable; the Person; the Witness; the Knower of the field; and the Indestructible;

sanskrit: yogo yogavidāṃ netā pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ nārasiṃhavapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: Yoga; the Leader of those who know yoga; the Lord of primal matter and spirit; he whose body is the Man-Lion; the Glorious; Keśava; the Supreme Person;

sanskrit: sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇur bhūtādir nidhir avyayaḥ saṃbhavo bhāvano bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhur īśvaraḥ
english: the All; Śarva; the Auspicious; the Steadfast Pillar; the Origin of beings; the imperishable Treasure; the Source; the Bringer-into-being; the Sustainer; the Wellspring; the Lord; the Sovereign;

sanskrit: svayaṃbhūḥ śaṃbhur ādityaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāsvanaḥ anādinidhano dhātā vidhātā dhātur uttamaḥ
english: the Self-existent; Śaṃbhu; the Sun; the Lotus-eyed; the Mighty-voiced; he without beginning or end; the Upholder; the Ordainer; the Highest of supports;

sanskrit: aprameyo hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābho 'maraprabhuḥ viśvakarmā manus tvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviro dhruvaḥ
english: the Immeasurable; Hṛṣīkeśa, lord of the senses; the Lotus-naveled; Lord of the immortals; the All-maker; Manu; Tvaṣṭṛ the shaper; the Most Massive; the Ancient; the Fixed;

sanskrit: agrāhyaḥ śāśvataḥ kṛṣṇo lohitākṣaḥ pratardanaḥ prabhūtas trikakubdhāma pavitraṃ maṅgalaṃ param
english: the Ungraspable; the Eternal; Kṛṣṇa; the Red-eyed; the Destroyer; the Abundant; he whose abode is the three quarters; the Pure; the supreme Auspiciousness.
